          Como vs Man Utd Prediction: Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      Jonathan Davies / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Wednesday's Champions League clash at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with our Como vs Man Utd prediction and preview. Can the Red Devils end their winless streak?
Manchester United will look to ease the pressure on Michael Carrick and put their recent struggles behind them when they resume their Champions League campaign against Como.

Following Sunday's 1-1 draw with cross-Pennine rivals Leeds United, in which Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo‘s first-half effort, Carrick has now overseen a six-match winless run in all competitions (D3 L3).
The Red Devils have been unable to build on the momentum of their 4-0 rout of Sabah on Matchday 1, beaten 2-0 by Atlético Madrid in Spain last week.

Pablo Barrios struck after just 47 seconds as United conceded in the opening minute of a Champions League game for only the fourth time – also doing so against Juventus in October 1997, Barcelona in November 1998, and Basel in November 2002.

Leny Yoro was sent off for a professional foul in the 74th minute – meaning he will miss Wednesday's trip to Italy – before Ademola Lookman condemned the Red Devils to their sixth defeat in nine Champions League matches (W1 D2).
Man Utd only lost 21% of their 190 matches in the competition under Alex Ferguson (W102 D49 L39). Since his retirement, though, they have been beaten in 38% of their 56 games (W24 D11 L21).

Last week's reverse at the Metropolitano also marked a sixth defeat in 10 Champions League outings away from Old Trafford (W1 D2), while they have only kept a single clean sheet in their last 15 such matches on the road (a 2-0 victory over Villarreal in November 2021).

United did have their chances in Madrid, though. They created four big chances without scoring any, their most without scoring in a Champions League game since September 2012 against Galatasaray (also 0/4).

Carrick will be looking for inspiration in Lombardy from the likes of Marcus Rashford, who could make his 50th Champions League appearance (34 for Man Utd, four for Aston Villa, 11 for Barcelona). Harry Kane (34), Raheem Sterling (20) and Andrew Cole (18) are the only English players to better Rashford's tally of 17 goals in their first 50 games in the competition.
Meanwhile, Como and Cesc Fàbregas will hope Assane Diao can shine again following his impressive start to the Champions League campaign.

After scoring in the 4-1 win over RB Leipzig and last week's 3-2 defeat at Feyenoord, the Senegal international became only the third player to find the net in an Italian club's opening two Champions League matches, after Alessandro Del Piero for Juventus in 1995, and former Man Utd striker Edinson Cavani for Napoli in 2011.
At 21 years and 37 days old, Diao also became the youngest African player to find the target in both his first two appearances in the competition.
However, his exploits last week in Rotterdam were not enough to prevent Como from becoming the 10th successive Italian side to fail to win their first away game in the Champions League (D4 L6).

I Lariani did make history, though, as only the second team not to name a single player from their own nation in the starting XI for either of their first two matches in the competition, after Sheriff Tiraspol in 2021-22.

Yet, Italy under-21 international Mattia Liberali did his hopes of featuring from the start on Matchday 3 no harm on Sunday, as he scored in a 3-1 victory at Fiorentina that ended his side's three-game winless streak in all competitions.

The only negative from Florence was the early withdrawal of Trevoh Chalobah, who faces a race to be fit for this game, with Fàbregas' side looking to become only the second Italian team after Lazio in 1999-2000 to win their first two home games in the European Cup/Champions League.

This will be the first ever meeting between Como and Man Utd, but it is not the first time the two coaches have faced off in the competition. The former midfield maestros were on opposing sides as players in the 2008-09 semi-finals, with Carrick and United beating Fàbregas' Arsenal 4-1 on aggregate.

Since the start of last season, there have been six meetings between English and Italian sides in the Champions League. The Premier League team has prevailed on five occasions, with the exception being Atalanta's 2-1 win over Chelsea in the league phase last term.
The Opta supercomputer marginally favours a Como victory, with the Serie A side given a 41.7% chance.
